The resected tissue is sent for pathological examination to confirm or rule out malignancy and determine the extent of the disease. The procedure is quite challenging and carries a significant risk of post-operative complications. For example, patients might experience serious bleeding or damage to the liver, which sometimes need more surgeries to repair.  The success rate varies greatly depending on the skill of the surgeon and the patients overall health.
